item.title: AIs as Modern Genies
item.description: This essay was written with Barath Raghavan, and originally appeared in Lawfare. In April, an artificial intelligence (AI) agent conducting a routine task at a company hit a snag, tried to solve it, and soon ended up deleting the company’s database along with all of its backups. In July, OpenAI asked an unreleased AI model to attempt a hacking test. Instead of staying in the isolated box the developers had put it in, the model hacked onto the open internet and into another company to steal the answers. And as reported in August, an AI agent booked someone into a full gym class by ......

item.description: A vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances could allow an authenticated attacker with valid credentials for a user account with the role of user or admin or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access to an affected device to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks and execute unauthorized software. This vulnerability is due to the availability of memory write commands in the UEFI Shell while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled on a device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by selecting the UE...

item.title: Cisco Secure Email Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions Ciphertext Decryption Vulnerabilities
item.description: Multiple vulnerabilities in the Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) decryption functionality of Cisco Secure Email could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to recover plain text from encrypted email messages. These vulnerabilities are due to insufficient validation of message integrity. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by using a machine-in-the-middle technique to intercept and modify traffic between email gateways. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to obtain plaintext content from the encrypted communication. There are no workarounds that ad...

item.title: Stealing AI Reasoning Traces
item.description: Interesting research: “Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs“: Abstract: Leading large language model providers now conceal their models’ step-by-step reasoning, or chain-of-thought, to protect intellectual property and limit information leakage. Rather than storing these traces server-side, providers return them to the client as blocks of encrypted text, which the client passes back with each subsequent request. Building on prior research, we identify an architectural vulnerability: these encrypted blocks are fully compatible and interchangeable across different sessions, users,...

item.title: Testing race conditions with memory access tracing and stack-based delay injection
item.description: Many security bugs are race conditions, where multi-threaded execution has to occur with the right interleaving for a negative effect to appear. This creates challenges for several use cases: Confirming bug candidates that have been discovered manually or through static analysis. Regression tests: After fixing a race condition bug, there is often no good way to write a regression test that reliably triggers the bug as part of a test suite. Automatic bug discovery, such as fuzzing: It is hard for a fuzzer to exercise all interesting interleavings of concurrent operations, or reach code paths th...

item.title: AIs Compress Exploit Timeline
item.description: Give an AI agent a mere rumor of an exploit, and it’s enough for them to find it. What’s worse, I found I could use my own agents to find the exploit just by knowing roughly what it was about and so could have been exploiting it well before the public patch was available! Given that just the rumour of a security issue seems enough to give attackers enough info to find new exploits, we’re going to need to change the way we deal with security responses in open source. Simon Willison comments: Anil points out that this rate of discovery appears incompatible with existing open source embargo pract...

item.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Rotting Squid on a Beached California Boat
item.description: Smells awful: But an estimated 30 to 50 tons of dead squid remain inside the boat’s catch tank, where they have been decomposing for days. “That is nasty. I wouldn’t want to do that,” said commercial fisherman Dick Ogg of the Bodega Bay Fishermen’s Marketing Association. Ogg said anyone familiar with the fishing industry understands what happens when a large catch sits for an extended period. “If you think about what happens after four or five days, it’s a gooey mess,” he said. The odor has become a defining feature of the operation, and the beach remains closed to the public while crews work...

item.title: Microsoft’s Patching
item.description: Once a month, Microsoft pushes a security update to all Windows users. Tomorrow’s is a new record: Microsoft’s patch for September is a doozy, with a record number of roughly 972 vulnerabilities fixed and 112 of them meeting the high critical-severity threshold. It was only two months ago that Microsoft patched a then-record 570 vulnerabilities. Then, last month, Microsoft patched some 620 of them. Google and other companies have also published record numbers of vulnerabilities in recent months. Two weeks ago, OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, and 100 companies and org...

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted email message that contains malicious SQL statements through an affected device. item.title: 25 Years of Mass Surveillance Is Enough
item.description: This essay was written with Cindy Cohn, and originally appeared in Lawfare. One of the many legacies of the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11 is the government-wide shift from targeted surveillance—such as individual wiretaps or pen register/trap and trace orders—to mass surveillance techniques—such as tapping into the internet backbone or mass collection of telephone or internet metadata. The legal and technical architecture of modern mass surveillance, initially framed as a necessary defense against terrorist threats, has grown far beyond that justification and national security in general. Mass...

New Attack Against RSA
item.description: ArsTechnica is reporting on a “new” attack against RSA, one that bypasses factoring. First, this attack isn’t new. The original research is from 2007. What is new is the implementation. Second, it is a forgery attack. It allows an attacker to forge digital signatures. It does not recover the private key from the public key. Third, the attack only works against pure signatures. That is, signatures without any formatting or padding. This is not generally how we use RSA in practice. Fourth, speed is all relative. This is not a polynomial-time algorithm; it’s a subexponential-time algorithm. But i...

item.title: I Want Better Reporting on AI Genie Behavior
item.description: AI systems are regularly completing tasks in ways that their prompters don’t want or intend. Some of them are disturbing, and some of them are dangerous. This is something I’ve been calling “genie behavior,” because I think that really gets at the core of what’s happening. I wish the popular press would report on this better. I don’t like the “going rogue” framing because it deflects the responsibility from the prompters—often the AI companies themselves. item.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
item.description: This is a problem: Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it’s a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We have abliterated models in the title because it’s the most popular reason people download modified weights without verifying what’s inside. Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model’s ability to refuse. You find the direction in the weights that carries “no” and subtract it. The model then answers things a safety-tuned version would turn down. It began as a research trick and it’s now routine before people up...

item.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
item.description: Interesting research: Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2384, or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. Interesting research: TL;DR: Chinese AI models now sit inside Western products, and some carry geopolitical triggers: tell the model who the code is for, and the security of what it writes changes. For the first time, we showed that this vulnerability lives in the model’s weights, and that removing the model’s CCP alignment removes it.
One word tilts the code against Americans. Ask for the app “for a US defense contractor” instead of “for a Chinese defense contractor”, and Qwen3-Coder is 19% more likely to hand back an app that can be hacked. ......

item.title: ZDI-26-829: (0Day) (Pwn2Own) Alpine iLX-F511 Bluetooth OBEX Packet Handling Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: This vulnerability allows physically present attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Alpine iLX-F511 devices. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The ZDI has assigned a CVSS rating of 6.8. The following CVEs are assigned: CVE-2026-118611.

item.title: Linux kernel RCE CVE-2026-98432
item.description:
CVSSv3 Score:
9.8
CVE-2026-98432:ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it. item.title: USN-9000-1: Twisted vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Twisted's IMAP server mishandled wildcard patterns in mailbox list commands. An authenticated remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Twisted to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service.

item.description: It was discovered that Squid incorrectly handled certain HTTP Transfer- Encoding headers. An attacker could possibly use this issue to perform HTTP request smuggling attacks, bypass security mechanisms, or poison web caches.

item.description: It was discovered that Net-SNMP incorrectly handled newly accepted connections in the SMUX module. An unauthenticated remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Net-SNMP to block indefinitely, resulting in a denial of service.

item.title: USN-8996-1: APT vulnerability
item.description: Max Justicz discovered that APT incorrectly handled hard links when encountering redirects and retrying package downloads. A remote on-path attacker could possibly use this issue to trick APT into installing an unverified package and achieve remote code execution with root privileges.

item.title: Pinpointing Location of Videos from Background Airplane Sounds
item.description: This is fascinating: The video describes a technique that can reveal where an otherwise unidentifiable recording was made by analyzing its audio for the faint sounds of passing aircraft. The technique is both fascinating and frightening. It works by looking at Doppler curves, which plot the way a plane’s sound changes as it passes overhead because of the Doppler effect. This is the same familiar Doppler effect that causes the frequency of a siren to rise as it approaches and then fall as it passes by and moves away. item.title: The code and the court: Why your email security thinks like Napoleon
item.description: In 1804, Napoleon gave France a code that much of the world still runs on. The Code civil replaced a tangle of local customs with a single written statute: orderly and knowable. In that tradition, the judge’s job, in Montesquieu’s phrase, is to be the mouth of the law, nothing more. Certainty was the point. Certainty has a cost. A codified system is only as current as its code. When the world produces something the code did not anticipate — a new technology, a new fraud — there is no statute to apply, and everyone waits for someone to write one. Your email security works exactly this way...

item.description:
An October cyberattack on refrigeration controllers at about 700 French retail sites was carried out by a cyber unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the French government said yesterday.
The attackers broke into controllers on the night of October 11 and changed their defrost settings to high temperatures. That caused food losses and, in at least 15 cases, fires.

item.title: When everything is a threat, nothing feels safe
item.description: When you leave home, you lock the door. When you get into the car, you fasten your seat belt. These are familiar safety habits. We understand their purpose, know how to perform them and rarely need to stop and think about them. Our digital lives are different. We shop, bank, work and keep in touch with family and friends online, often without clear signs of where a danger begins or which precaution matters most. We receive a steady stream of warnings about new scams, stolen credentials, data breaches and software vulnerabilities. The messages vary in urgency, but many seem to demand our i...

item.description:

item.title: CVE-2026-100223 Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system.
To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system.
The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files....

item.title: CVE-2026-95947 Windows Error Reporting Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Windows Error Reporting (WER) when WER handles and executes files. The vulnerability could allow elevation of privilege if an attacker can successfully exploit it.
An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could gain greater access to sensitive information and system functionality. To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker could run a specially crafted application.
The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting the way that WER handles and executes files....

item.title: CVE-2026-94525 Windows Error Reporting Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Windows Error Reporting (WER) when WER handles and executes files. The vulnerability could allow elevation of privilege if an attacker can successfully exploit it.
An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could gain greater access to sensitive information and system functionality. To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker could run a specially crafted application.
The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting the way that WER handles and executes files....

item.title: CVE-2026-105545 Windows Installer Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Windows Installer when the Windows Installer fails to properly sanitize input leading to an insecure library loading behavior.
A locally authenticated attacker could run arbitrary code with elevated system privileges. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights.
The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting the input sanitization error to preclude unintended elevation....

item.title: iOS Sandbox Escape Is Public, and Apple Hasn’t Confirmed a Fix
item.description: A public iOS sandbox escape could expose wallet keys, Binance warns. No attacks are reported and no fix is confirmed. A local attacker with hypervisor access could possibly use this to trigger an out-of-bounds condition and compromise the integrity of SEV-SNP guest memory. (CVE-2023-20585)
Several security issues were discovered in the Linux kernel. An attacker could possibly use these to compromise the system. This update corrects flaws in the following subsystems: - USB Gadget drivers; - Memory management; - NVDIMM (Non-Volatile Memory Device) drivers; - N...

item.title: USN-8952-3: Tornado regression
item.description:
USN-8952-2 fixed a regression in Tornado that broke static file serving for applications that subclass Tornado's StaticFileHandler, such as Jupyter. Unfortunately, that update's incomplete fix could introduce a regression by rejecting symlinks into system directories like /usr/share, which distribution packages use for their JavaScript and fonts, causing web UIs to return 403 errors. This update fixes the problem.
We apologize for the inconvenience.

item.description: As AI model training and distillation increase, AI tokens are becoming a piping hot currency for threat actors. Cloud hosting provider Railway found out the hard way; it has confirmed a near 26-hour battle against attackers targeting AI provider credentials to sell to AI ‘transfer stations’ for use in model distillation. The crooks generated about $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage charges using the stolen credentials and potentially had access to up to 100,000 workspace credentials. item.title: Smashing Security podcast #492: How hackers turned Russian cars into pumpkins
item.description:
You're driving your new Chinese SUV when the dashboard goes dark. Ten minutes later, your phone rings. A stranger says they've got the digital key to your car, and would you like it back? Of course you would. That'll be $550.
Meanwhile, three men have been charged over a scheme that used deepfakes of company bosses to steal around $130 million. Hear more about what happened, and the simple human trick that can foil the fakes.
All this and more in episode 492 of the "Smashing Security" podcast with cybersecurity expert and keynote speaker Graham Cluley, and special guest Danny Palmer....

item.title: Attackers leverage AntiFox platform on Alibaba cloud to target aws environments

item.title: USN-9063-1: Yodl vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Yodl incorrectly handled certain input, leading to a buffer over-read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Yodl to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

item.title: USN-9062-1: SNMPTT vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that SNMPTT did not properly sanitize trap data passed to commands run through the EXEC, PREEXEC, and unknown_trap_exec options. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary shell commands.

item.title: USN-9060-1: kramdown vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that kramdown processed the template option in documents by default. An attacker could possibly use this issue to read arbitrary files or execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9059-1: ruby-jwt vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that ruby-jwt incorrectly verified HMAC signatures when the verification key was empty or missing. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to forge tokens and bypass authentication.

item.title: USN-9058-1: Action Pack Page Caching vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Action Pack Page Caching incorrectly handled certain request paths when writing cached pages. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to write arbitrary files to the web server, and possibly execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9057-1: rkhunter vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that rkhunter downloaded mirror updates over an insecure channel. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9056-1: Prosody Community Modules vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that the LDAP authentication modules in Prosody Community Modules did not fully verify XMPP addresses when checking for administrator privileges. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to gain administrator privileges.

item.title: USN-9055-1: pecl_http vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that pecl_http incorrectly handled certain HTTP request parameters, leading to a type confusion. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause PHP to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9054-1: Babel vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Babel incorrectly evaluated certain code during compilation when used with certain plugins. If a user or an automated system were tricked into compiling specially crafted code, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9053-1: NetworkManager-ssh vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that NetworkManager-ssh did not properly validate extra options in VPN connection settings. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to escalate privileges.

item.description: A Microsoft research project combining AI agents with human security researchers uncovered 59 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including bugs that had survived in production code for more than 20 years. item.description:

The company has already applied mitigations against attacks between VMs, and between VMs and the host. Inside a VM, the flaws may let an attacker with code on the same processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel.

item.title: USN-9068-1: Debian-LAN vulnerability
item.description: Wolfgang Schweer discovered that Debian-LAN configured overly permissive ACLs for the Kerberos admin server. An authenticated user could possibly use this issue to change the credentials of other users, leading to privilege escalation.

item.title: USN-9089-1: x11vnc vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that x11vnc created shared memory segments with insecure permissions. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information or modify screen contents.

item.title: USN-9088-1: TigerVNC vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that the TigerVNC viewer stored TLS certificate exceptions as trusted certificate authorities. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to impersonate any VNC server after a user had added a certificate exception for the attacker's server.

item.title: USN-9087-1: signing-party vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that the gpg-key2ps tool in signing-party did not properly sanitize user IDs before passing them to a shell. If a user were tricked into processing a specially crafted OpenPGP key, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary commands.

item.title: USN-9086-1: SA-Exim vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that SA-Exim unsafely evaluated the parameters of its greylisting SpamAssassin rule. An attacker able to write SpamAssassin configuration files or rules could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9085-1: Ruby OpenID vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Ruby OpenID sent a request to the claimed identifier URL before verifying the signature of an OpenID response. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform server-side request forgery attacks.

item.title: USN-9084-1: Radicale vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Radicale did not delay failed authentication attempts when using htpasswd authentication. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain user passwords through timing or brute-force attacks.

item.title: USN-9083-1: gevent vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that the gevent WSGI server incorrectly validated chunked transfer encoding trailers in HTTP requests. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform HTTP request smuggling attacks, leading to privilege escalation.

item.title: USN-9082-1: pngquant vulnerability
item.description: Choi Jaeseung discovered that pngquant incorrectly handled certain PNG images, leading to a buffer overflow. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause pngquant to crash or execute arbitrary code.

item.description:
You join a video call, and your contact and a few colleagues are already there, waiting patiently. But they can't hear you, and a pop-up says you need to install an update to fix your microphone. What could possibly go wrong?
Meanwhile, we explain how changing just a handful of numbers can turn an AI model into a sleeper agent, waiting for the right moment to strike.
Plus, Andrius Buinovskis of NordLayer explains how companies can see which AI tools their staff are really using, and stop sensitive data leaking out, without banning AI altogether.

item.title: USN-9188-1: OAuthLib vulnerabilities
item.description:
It was discovered that OAuthLib incorrectly handled JSONP callback parameters in the token revocation endpoint. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code in a client application. (CVE-2026-49264)
Elvin Latifli discovered that OAuthLib incorrectly compared PKCE code verifiers, using a comparison that was not constant-time. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain access tokens, resulting in an account takeover. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-49265)

item.title: Smashing Security podcast #494: The Russian accused of spying on Palantir from Starbucks
item.description:
A would-be spy is recruited on Telegram for $15,000 and sent halfway around the world to snoop on Palantir. His cover story when he's caught? He wanted to ask a woman out on a date.
Meanwhile, Carl Miller investigates a think tank with 300 experts on its books, one of whom is the inconveniently dead Henry Kissinger. But who is its real audience? You might be surprised.
Plus, Coreview's Andrea Sivieri explains why Microsoft Copilot is brilliant at finding anything in your company, including the salary spreadsheet someone shared with everybody back in 2019.

item.title: USN-9203-1: libpcap vulnerabilities
item.description:
Jin Wei, Kunwei Qian, and Ping Chen discovered that libpcap did not properly validate the format of MAC addresses passed to the pcap_ether_aton() function, leading to an out-of-bounds read and write. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause applications using libpcap to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-11961)
It was discovered that the libpcap remote capture (rpcap) client did not properly validate packet messages received from the server. A malicious server could po...

item.description: It was discovered that Speex incorrectly handled oversize input when appending data to a bit buffer not owned by the library. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Speex to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-102633)

item.description: It was discovered that Apache Commons BCEL incorrectly cached classes under their self-declared names without validating them against the requested name. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause BCEL to return or verify a different class than the one requested.

item.title: USN-9204-1: dav1d vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that dav1d incorrectly handled certain AV1 video streams with extremely large frame sizes. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause dav1d to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

item.title: UK’s long-awaited National Cyber Action Plan delayed until December
item.description: Officials, who had planned to publish the document in mid-November, now aim to unveil the strategy for defending the wider economy against state-backed and criminal hackers on December 9.

item.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
item.description: India’s Digital Infrastructure for Governance Impact and Transformation tool can leak data

item.title: USN-9016-2: Apache HTTP Server regression
item.description:
USN-9016-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Apache2. Unfortunately the upstream fix introduced a regression that prevented cookies being set during a redirect under certain circumstances. This update fixes the problem.
Original advisory details:
Zhang San, Ankit Prateek, Zhen Kong, SeungHyun Cho, Ryoma Nishioka, Keita Sode and Hyojae Lee discovered that Apache HTTP Server did not correctly handle certain memory operations. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 14.04 LTS, Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubun...

item.title: USN-9214-1: GNU binutils vulnerabilities
item.description:
It was discovered that the GNU binutils gold linker incorrectly handled certain ELF files. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2019-1010204)
Han Zheng discovered that GNU binutils incorrectly handled demangling certain Rust symbols. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2022-27943)

item.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
item.description:
A website can look perfectly fine to the person running it. Log out, visit the same page, and things might look different. item.title: USN-9206-1: Guava vulnerabilities
item.description:
It was discovered that Guava did not correctly handle permissions for certain temporary directories. An attacker could possibly use this issue to read or modify sensitive information. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2020-8908, CVE-2023-2976)
Kaya Emre Arikan discovered that Guava did not correctly handle deserializing certain data. If a user or automated system were tricked into opening a specially crafted file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-102554)...
